cms.support: Open source; developed by the WordPress community and supported by Automattic and other contributors.
cms.technology: PHP server-side language, MySQL or MariaDB database, and HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the front end.
cms.capabilities: Offers thousands of themes and plugins, a built-in content editor, blogging tools, user management, and a REST API. Supports websites ranging from personal blogs to large publications.
cms.limitations: Plugins can introduce security vulnerabilities or compatibility problems. Websites require regular software, theme, and plugin updates. Extensive customization may require PHP knowledge.

cms.support: Open source; maintained by the Drupal community and supported by contributors and commercial development companies.
cms.technology: PHP server-side language with MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite databases. Uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the front end.
cms.capabilities: Provides customizable content types, themes, modules, user permissions, multilingual support, and API integration. Suitable for large and complex websites.
cms.limitations: Has a steeper learning curve than many other CMS platforms. Advanced customization often requires programming experience. Updates and module compatibility can require technical maintenance.

cms.support: Free and open source; maintained by the Open Source Matters organization and the Joomla community.
cms.technology: PHP server-side language with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL databases. Uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the front end.
cms.capabilities: Supports templates, extensions, user access controls, multilingual websites, content management, and built-in menu management.
cms.limitations: Can be more difficult for beginners to learn than simpler website builders. Some advanced features require third-party extensions, which may introduce compatibility and maintenance issues.

cms.support: Open source; developed and maintained by the Ghost Foundation. Also offers managed hosting through Ghost(Pro).
cms.technology: Node.js server-side platform with a MySQL database. Uses JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with Handlebars for themes.
cms.capabilities: Provides publishing tools, customizable themes, membership management, paid subscriptions, newsletters, and an API for connecting external applications.
cms.limitations: Primarily designed for publishing and membership websites rather than general-purpose websites. Has fewer extensions than WordPress, and custom functionality may require programming knowledge.

cms.support: Open source headless CMS developed by Strapi, Inc. with a commercial cloud hosting option.
cms.technology: Node.js server-side platform using JavaScript or TypeScript. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, and SQLite databases.
cms.capabilities: Provides customizable content types, an administrative content editor, user permissions, plugins, and REST and GraphQL APIs. Allows developers to connect content to different front-end applications.
cms.limitations: Does not provide a traditional built-in website front end or theme system. Requires developers to build or connect a separate front end. MongoDB is not supported.
